note: Attacker-controlled CoAP/TCP packet's first byte determines header size (2, 3, 4, or 6 bytes) based on the 4-bit length nibble.
Header size is checked against the PDU's max_hdr_size, but no check ensures the token area is large enough for the extended token length bytes that follow.
PDU buffer is resized to hold only the payload after the header; the token bytes are expected to be within the resized region.

code: if (pdu->token - hdr_size != data) memcpy(pdu->token - hdr_size, data, length);
note: Input bytes are copied into the PDU buffer starting at token-hdr_size; the token pointer is positioned after the header.
The computed header size is stored in the PDU; for TCP with len nibble 15, hdr_size is 6 but the actual message may be shorter.
coap_pdu_parse_header is invoked with the PDU whose token pointer may point near the end of the allocated buffer when the input is very short.
hdr points to the start of the header in the PDU buffer; for a 6-byte TCP header with only 1-5 input bytes, this points before the copied data.
For TCP/TLS protocol, reads hdr[hdr_size-1] which is hdr[5] for a 6-byte header; if the input was shorter than 6 bytes, this reads beyond the copied buffer.
Reads hdr[0] which is the first byte of the header; for a 6-byte TCP header with only 1 byte of input, this reads from uninitialized or out-of-bounds heap memory.
When e_token_length nibble is 13 (extended 1-byte token length), reads pdu->token[0] which may be beyond the allocated buffer if the input length was only the header size.
When e_token_length nibble is 14 (extended 2-byte token length), reads pdu->token[0] and pdu->token[1] which may be beyond the allocated buffer, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ.
